what_is_checked: gate-encode: type 0 returns the zeroed OK status at once (events gate_type + return_ok_zeroed, nothing installed); every other type byte encodes as its 4-byte little-endian PutFixed32 and proceeds; the gate is independent of manual_flush_/recycle

emit-failure: a nonzero emit code clears compression_type_ to 0, installs nothing, allocates nothing, skips the Flush, and returns the emit status (code/subcode/flags/state carried through the copy rule)

emit-ok + manual_flush_ == 0: dest_->Flush() is called with (dest_.get(), IO_TOTAL = 4) and its status moves into s (old emit state_ delete[]'d when non-null; source code/subcode/scope/state_ reset per the IOStatus move-assignment); manual_flush_ == 1 skips the Flush and keeps the emit status

flush-failure-still-installs: a nonzero Flush status does NOT block the install -- the Create call, the compress_ install and the buffer allocation all still run, and the returned status is the Flush error (upstream checks s.ok() once, before the Flush)

create-install: type 7 installs a non-null product; every other type installs null (the factory gate) but STILL allocates the fresh buffer; buffer size is 0x7ff9 (legacy, recycle == 0) or 0x7ff5 (recyclable, recycle == 1); a previous buffer is delete[]'d, a previous compress_ is overwritten without a delete (leak on re-entry)

CORRECTION to merged RE-001-zstd-compress-cache-115: 0x6051a20 is WritableFileWriter::Flush (census-confirmed, 2908 B), not a 'shared 4-byte copy helper'. The call at 0x5f04394 passes (sret, dest_.get(), IO_TOTAL); the callee reads WritableFileWriter members and clocks.

Flush-failure-still-installs: after dest_->Flush() the binary jumps straight to the Create section (0x5f042af) without re-checking the status code. Upstream log_writer.cc checks s.ok() once, before the Flush, and the init block runs unconditionally inside it -- so a failed Flush still installs the compressor and the buffer, and the returned status is the Flush error.

Status byte rules, now explained from upstream: the returned 16-byte status is IOStatus (Status layout code@0, subcode@1, sev_@2, retryable@3, data_loss@4, scope@5, state_@8, status.h:841-857). The final copy zeroes byte 2 because IOStatus's copy-ctor builds from Status(code, subcode), which initializes sev_ to kNoError (io_status.h:311, status.h:866-878). The Flush move does not touch byte 2 because IOStatus's move-assignment does not mention sev_ (io_status.h:371-405); its source resets (bytes 0-1 to kOk/kNone, byte 5 to kIOErrorScopeFileSystem = 0, bytes 8-15 moved) match the binary's move instruction for instruction. Bytes 6-7 are padding, never written by this routine.
The return copy transfers the state_ pointer with a plain 8-byte move (no CopyState call in the body); the stack slot's state_ is not freed afterwards in this function -- the returned status owns it.
The early-OK path (type == 0) writes bytes 0-3, 4-5, 8-15 as zero and also leaves bytes 6-7 untouched, the same padding rule as the copy path.

The template's tail padding (+0x29..+0x2f, 7 bytes) is never written; Create reads only the named fields, so the padding is don't-care -- but a byte-exact template replay must mark those bytes unwritten, not zero.

No block_offset_ check: the binary never reads this+0x08, so the upstream assert(block_offset_ == 0) is compiled out -- a caller could invoke the routine mid-block and it would still emit the type-9 record.
The sbb trick for max_output_len: cmpb $1, recycle; sbb r15,r15; and $4; add $0x7ff5 gives 0x7ff9 when recycle == 0 and 0x7ff5 when recycle == 1 (kBlockSize 32768 minus header 7 or 11).

The one caller DBImpl::CreateWAL builds the Writer with the move ctor and stores it through the Writer** out-param before calling this routine; the routine therefore always runs on a fresh Writer with compress_ == null and compressed_buffer_ == null, so the old-value branches (leak old compress_, delete[] old buffer) are unreachable in the one real call path but are modelled for completeness.
ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter echoes the set value on success (201 -> 1 returns 1, verified live against system libzstd 1.5.5); it is not an error code. The live engine check asserts only !isError(ret).
